deed: הברון רוטשילד תמך בהתיישבות היהודית בארץ והיה מרכזי בהקמת תעשיית היין
title: Baron Rothschild supported the first colonies and built the wineries from which Carmel Winery grew

trailer.text: Baron Edmond de Rothschild, one of the wealthiest French Jews of his day, became known as the Well-Known Benefactor and the Father of the Yishuv for his support of the Jewish community in the Land of Israel.

According to the Foundation, after the riots against the Jews of Russia he was convinced to support the Jews who had chosen to settle in the Land of Israel, and he began with a donation to the colony of Rishon LeZion, which was about to be dismantled.
According to ynet, the settlers asked him for help in creating jobs in grape growing, and he funded grapevine saplings and sent instructors from France.
According to the Foundation, he purchased about 500 square kilometers of land in the Land and established dozens of colonies, factories and wineries.

According to a sponsored article on ynet, written in cooperation with Superbrands to mark 135 years since the winery was founded, Rothschild supported the establishment of Carmel's two large historic wineries, in Rishon LeZion and in Zikhron Ya'akov, and at the time of writing Carmel Winery produced about 12 million bottles a year ‹c28›.

stations.title: Before: Riots in Russia and Colonies in Difficulty

paragraphs.text: According to JTA, the riots in Southern Russia, which broke out in 1881, brought many refugees to Constantinople and aroused the Baron's interest in the Land of Israel.
According to the Foundation, in the wake of the riots against the Jews of Russia the Baron, at the age of 35, was convinced that the Jews who had chosen to settle in the Land should be supported.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the pioneers of Rishon LeZion were not prepared for agricultural life, and lacked even the basic capabilities to succeed in it.
According to the same newspaper, in Zikhron Ya'akov the attempts to cultivate the land met with almost total failure, and many died from malaria or were blinded by eye diseases.
According to ynet, the shortage of employment at that time was great.

stations.title: The Well-Known Benefactor: The First Money

paragraphs.text: According to the Foundation, the Baron's involvement in the colonies began with a donation to Rishon LeZion, which was about to be dismantled.
According to JTA, Yosef Feinberg, leader of the pioneers of Rishon LeZion, obtained money from the Baron so that the settlers could overcome their difficulties.
The sources differ on the amount.
According to mako, Rabbi Mohilever met the Baron in Paris and convinced him to fund the establishment of an agricultural colony for families who had immigrated from Russia and Poland.
According to the Foundation, the name the Well-Known Benefactor became attached to him in his first years because he refused to publicize his name as a donor.

According to the Foundation, the Baron's activity expanded and included purchasing land, economic development of the colonies, and establishing an infrastructure for educational, health and other institutions.
According to the Foundation, he purchased about 500 square kilometers of land in the Land and established dozens of colonies, factories and wineries.
On exactly how many colonies, and how much money was invested in total, the sources say different things.
According to the Foundation, the Baron made five journeys to the Land of Israel, and on each one he brought a team of experts and professional equipment.
According to Ramat Hanadiv, he made the first journey in April 1887, at the age of 41.
According to the Foundation, after 18 years of direct support the Baron transferred the administration of the colonies to the ICA.
According to the Encyclopedia, the transfer covered about 250,000 dunams and a network of 12 colonies, most of which were ready to be independent thanks to his support.
According to the Foundation, the Baron later established PICA, headed by his son, James Armand de Rothschild.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Baron Rothschild's first visits to the Land of Israel (1887, 1893, 1899) were devoted to tours of the settlements.
According to ynet, the first settlers turned to the Baron and asked him to help them create jobs in grape growing.
According to JTA, when grain cultivation proved somewhat of a failure, the Baron established vineyards under the direction of experts.

According to the Jerusalem Post, the Baron immediately arranged for students of the Mikveh Israel agricultural school to train the settlers of Rishon LeZion, and in addition sent his own agricultural experts, who determined that the land in the area was suitable for growing grapes and trained some of the pioneers to tend the vineyards ‹c23›.
According to the Kosher Wine website, the Baron's representatives discovered that the Zikhron Ya'akov area has a climate similar to that of Bordeaux.
According to ynet, the help included learning the field, funding grapevine saplings and sending instructors from France.
According to Wine With Seth, the Bordeaux experts Gerard Ermens and Professor Gayon were brought in as the key technical experts.

According to Adam Montefiore of Carmel Winery, the cellars at Rishon LeZion cost the Baron 6 million francs and those at Zikhron Ya'akov 5 million, while the purchase of Château Lafite cost the Rothschild family 4 million francs.

stations.title: The Cellars in Rishon LeZion and Zikhron Ya'akov

paragraphs.text: According to ynet, Rothschild supported the establishment of Carmel's two large historic wineries, in Rishon LeZion and in Zikhron Ya'akov.
According to JTA, he built large wine cellars in Rishon LeZion, and when no market was found for the wine, he took the entire product from the settlers.
The Rishon Le Zion winery was built in 1890 by Baron Edmond de Rothschild.
According to ynet, the first telephone in Israel and the first connection to electricity were at Carmel Winery.
Carmel Wine Co. was founded to export the wines of Rishon Le Zion and Zichron Yaakov.
According to Wine With Seth, wine from Rishon LeZion won a gold medal at the 1900 Paris Exhibition, alongside Lafite and Margaux.
Wine With Seth: 1891

stations.title: From the Baron to the Winegrowers, and to This Day

paragraphs.text: According to ynet, in 1957 James Rothschild, son of the Well-Known Benefactor, transferred ownership of the wineries to the Winegrowers' Association.
According to ynet, the winery in Zikhron Ya'akov is the oldest active commercial winery in the country.
Carmel is the largest winery in Israel; according to Storenext data published by Calcalist, in May 2026 it held a volume market share of about 31.5%.

According to Decanter and Israel21c, Carmel Winery's Kayoumi Single Vineyard Shiraz 2008 won the international trophy at the 2010 Decanter World Wine Awards, in the category of red Rhône varietals over £10.
ynet: about 12 million

stations.title: Father of the Yishuv: Recognition and Farewell

paragraphs.text: According to the encyclopedia, the Baron became the central address for all the problems of the Yishuv, until he became known as the Father of the Yishuv.
According to the Encyclopedia, he won the appreciation and admiration of all sectors of the Yishuv and of the Zionist Organization.
According to JTA, High Commissioner Herbert Samuel said that the Baron was the benefactor of Jews and Arabs alike.
According to JTA, in the first years of political Zionism the Baron held aloof from it, fearing that it might interfere with his plans.
According to the Encyclopedia, he told Weizmann that without him the Zionists could have done nothing, and without the Zionists his work would have been dead.

According to JTA, he played an important part in the negotiations that resulted in the Balfour Declaration, and when the extended Jewish Agency was formed in August 1929 he was elected its honorary president.
According to the Foundation, the Baron passed away at the age of 89.
According to the Jerusalem Post, this was in 1934.
According to the Foundation, Ben-Gurion said in his eulogy that in the entire history of the Jewish people in the Diaspora it is hard to find a person who will compare to the image of the Baron.

According to the Foundation, Prime Minister Moshe Sharett said in the Knesset that the Baron did not appear as a generous person but as a liberator, liberating the masses from their exile and tracts of land from their desolation.
According to the Encyclopedia, in 1954 his remains and those of his wife were moved to Ramat HaNadiv, near Zikhron Ya'akov.

stations.title: Criticism: The Officials and the System

paragraphs.text: According to the Encyclopedia, the system of bureaucratic patronage was the greatest problem of the colonies for about 20 years, and aroused sharp criticism.
According to the Encyclopedia, the Baron's bureaucracy aroused sharp antagonism, which reached the level of revolt in several colonies.
According to the Encyclopedia, Ahad Ha'am denounced the Baron's system of settlement in his famous article.
According to the Jerusalem Post, there were those who thought the Baron interfered from afar too much in the day-to-day management of the Yishuv.
According to the same newspaper, the help to Zikhron Ya'akov came together with tyrannical officials.
According to the Jerusalem Post, many claim that the Baron himself did not know about the bad relations between the settlers and his officials.
According to the Encyclopedia, in retrospect the Baron's bureaucracy also played a positive role: it introduced new plant species and instructed the first settlers.

disagreements.question: When were the riots that roused the Baron?

versions.says: US Holocaust Memorial Museum: the wave of pogroms in Russia broke out in 1881 and lasted until 1884

According to the Foundation, in the wake of the riots against the Jews of Russia the Baron, at the age of 35, was convinced that the Jews who had chosen to settle in the Land of Israel should be supported.

disagreements.question: How much money did the Baron invest in total?

JTA: about $60 million
Wine With Seth: 11 million francs in Israeli wine alone

disagreements.question: How many colonies were established with his help?

versions.says: JTA (1934): over 30 colonies between 1880 and 1895
The Encyclopedia: he left behind almost 30 colonies and nearly 500,000 dunams

disagreements.question: When was the Rishon LeZion winery built?

versions.says: Kosher Wine: building had started by 1889, and the first section was completed in 1890
Wine With Seth: opened in 1890

disagreements.question: When was the Carmel company founded?

versions.says: Kosher Wine: 1896, to export wines
Jerusalem Post: the Baron founded the Carmel Winery in 1882

disagreements.question: Who transferred the wineries to the Winegrowers' Association, and when?

versions.says: ynet: James Rothschild, the Baron's son, in 1957
Adam Montefiore (Carmel): management of the wineries was handed to the growers as early as 1906, and they founded the cooperative
JTA (1934): in 1924, under the presidency of James de Rothschild
The Encyclopedia: at the end of 1923

disagreements.question: When did the Baron's wife die?

versions.says: The Foundation: his wife Ada died a few months after him and was buried beside him
Jerusalem Post: she died a year after him

disagreements.question: Was it Rothschild who founded the commercial wine industry in the Land?

versions.says: Wine With Seth: his intervention in 1882 transformed winemaking into a genuine commercial industry
Jerusalem Post: the Shor family's Zion Winery has a heritage that goes back to 1848, long before Carmel and the Baron

disagreements.question: Which is the oldest winery in Israel still operating?

versions.says: ynet (sponsored article): Carmel's winery in Zikhron Ya'akov is the oldest active commercial winery in the country
Adam Montefiore: Efrat Winery, founded by Zeev Zeida Teperberg in 1870, still operates today under the Teperberg name
Jerusalem Post: the Shor family's Zion Winery has made wine continuously since 1848

disagreements.question: When was the export company Carmel Wine Co. founded?

versions.says: Kosher Wine: in 1896, to export wines
Adam Montefiore (Carmel): in 1895, by E.Z. Lewin-Epstein; the first export office opened in Warsaw in 1896
eTurboNews: the company started operating in 1895
